# ReSharper `issues.xml` reconciliation — 2026-08-20

**Source:** user-supplied `/home/ubuntu/upload/issues.xml`, generated by JetBrains ReSharper 2024.1.3 for `Ricis.Core.sln`.
**Analyst extraction:** 723 issue instances across 13 projects. The highest severity class contains two `CSharpErrors` entries.
**Current compiler check:** `dotnet build Ricis.Core.csproj -c Release --no-restore` — **PASS, 0 warnings, 0 errors**, executed during `REMAINDER-2H-2026-08-20-01`.

## Reconciliation rule

A ReSharper `CSharpErrors` entry is not treated as a production defect solely because it exists in an older exported XML snapshot. It becomes an actionable code defect only when the current compiler, current test gate or a reproducible current analyzer run confirms it. The two highest-severity entries above are therefore preserved as historical evidence and are not “fixed” by changing working source code.

## Remaining issue inventory

The XML contains high-volume non-error findings, including 138 floating-point equality warnings, 122 `MergeIntoPattern` suggestions, 109 naming warnings, 46 non-accessed positional-property warnings, 38 redundant-using warnings and 17 unmatched checked-operator warnings. These are not silently bulk-fixed: each future code change requires semantic review, direct regression coverage where behavior can change, and a separate Analyst → Developer → QA cycle.

## XML warning preservation decisions

The `ConstantNullCoalescingCondition` warning at `Expressions/RicisComplexFunction.cs:133` was reviewed against `ParameterRebindingVisitorBase.Visit` and the direct `RicisComplexSuite` cases `CPLX01`–`CPLX07`. The `?? throw` guard is retained as a fail-closed contract: no deletion or simplification is authorized solely from the ReSharper warning. The same preservation rule applies to the corresponding null guards in expression and matrix classes until their nullability contract is formally proven and direct tests remain intact.

The previously reported `RedundantOverriddenMember` in `NumericalEvaluationSafety.cs:87` was not deleted. It was restored after the no-deletion incident and now has direct behavior coverage through `SAFE04`; its preservation and test evidence are recorded in the corrective sprint report.

## Explicit boundary

This reconciliation does not claim that all 723 findings are resolved. It resolves the highest-priority compiler question, records the safe preservation decision for the inspected null guard, and preserves the redundant override with direct coverage. The next XML-backed candidate must be selected by severity and semantic risk, not by raw issue count. No method, guard or contract member is deleted without caller graph, direct test, removal decision and owner approval.

## No-deletion preservation decisions

The `RedundantCast` finding in `RicisComplexFunction.Normalize` is preserved. `RicisPhasePipeline.Simplify(Expression)` returns `Expression`, while the contract requires `Expression<Func<T,T>>`; the cast is therefore a runtime type-boundary check, not a silent dead member. The `ConstantNullCoalescingCondition` guard in `RicisComplexFunction.Rebind` is also preserved pending a semantic nullability proof. No production member is removed or renamed without explicit owner approval.

## Additional warning audit

The `RedundantCast` at `Expressions/RicisSpecialExpressionRebinder.cs:25` is preserved. The cast documents and enforces the branch contract from an arbitrary `Expression` to `PoleInfinityExpression`; the surrounding special-node traversal is covered by `CS06` and `CS07`. No cast removal or suppression is authorized without a caller graph, runtime type proof, direct test, and owner approval.

The XML `ConstantConditionalAccessQualifier` and `ConstantNullCoalescingCondition` entries at the historical `RicisExpression.cs:35` location are stale relative to the current source location and contract. The current `GetHashCode` implementation intentionally retains `ToString()?.GetHashCode() ?? 0` as a fail-safe, and hash/equality behavior remains covered by `API11` and existing structural identity regressions. No nullable guard is removed without owner approval.

The XML `RedundantCast` candidate at `ExpressionExtensions.cs:313` was audited. The `(BigInteger)ul` cast is an explicit lossless conversion boundary from `ulong`, documenting the intended non-floating-point path; it is therefore preserved. Direct regression `API24` exercises a value above `Int64.MaxValue` and proves exact conversion. Full Core regression count is 390/390 after this coverage addition. No code deletion was performed.

The XML `CompareOfFloatsByEqualityOperator` findings were audited in the current code. Comparisons such as `value == 0.0`, `value == 1.0`, and `value == -1.0` are exact structural sentinel checks used by normalization, not approximate scientific comparisons. Existing direct coverage includes typed-zero simplification, indexed infinity handling, non-finite rejection, and vector invariants. Replacing these checks with epsilon logic would change symbolic semantics, so the findings are preserved; no production code is deleted.
